name: Grapefruit (White/Pink)
source_reference: Sawamura, 'Citrus Essential Oils', 2010; Shaw, J. Agric. Food Chem., 1979; Arctander, 'Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin', 1960
notes: Grapefruit oil is highly unstable and oxidizes rapidly. The characteristic bitter-sulfurous note is due to trace thioterpineol (para-menthene-8-thiol) at sub-ppm levels. Nootkatone, while at low concentration, has very low odor threshold and contributes significantly.

key_markers.5989-27-5: Limonene - dominant terpene carrier, provides basic citrus body
key_markers.4674-50-4: Nootkatone - sesquiterpene ketone defining grapefruit character; extremely low odor threshold (~1 ppb)
key_markers.71159-90-5: para-Menthene-8-thiol - the most powerful aroma compound known; defines characteristic grapefruit sulfurous tang at sub-ppb levels

olfactive_description: Bright, fresh, bittersweet citrus with a distinctive sulfurous-juicy top note unlike any other citrus. Clean, slightly tart, with a subtle bitter peel undertone and unique tropical-zesty sparkle.
